source: CloudResearch Connect, survey built in Engage. 10 approved participants, Nov 2 2026. Paid $0.75 each (estimated 5 min; median actual 9 min 42 s).

responses.likenessWhy: Looks same except picture is a fatter shorter face compared to real life
responses.storyWhy: Because it matches the words. Also it is the Jack and Bean Stalk story
responses.qualityWhy: Graphics wise that is what they look like.
responses.notGood: Not much, just double check the wizard has 6 digits total 5 fingers and 1 thumb. So it will be more realistic. (Follow-ups: 'common ai glitch', noticed when looking more closely, 'a minor distraction', nothing else.)

responses.likenessWhy: It's very similar - about as similar as a cartoon-style image could be
responses.storyWhy: It's the story I remember, obviously massively cut back to fit into 3 pages
responses.qualityWhy: I think there would be more words on each page if it was a proper book but other than that the style looks very professional
responses.notGood: I don't really like the last page where it talks about the person the character is modelled on - I didn't see the point in it. (Follow-ups: seemed unnecessary in the middle of the story; maybe have it as the first page; it would explain how/why the book was created before reading it.)

responses.likenessWhy: Had the same hair and glasses - same general look.
responses.storyWhy: They seemed to pretty much match up I thought
responses.qualityWhy: It looked pretty professional to me.
responses.notGood: It would look a little less Disney-like. (Follow-ups: the art style and the way the characters are drawn; 'nothing in particular, just not so Disney'; it doesn't affect how I connect with the characters.)

responses.likenessWhy: The AI came close in capturing the likeness of the real life person in this story.
responses.storyWhy: I needed the complete story for it to fully match. There was only part of the story here.
responses.qualityWhy: The look of the book looked like AI. It was not original looking.
responses.notGood: Include the entire story. Also I would want the book to be less 'AI slop' looking. (Follow-ups: the faces looked like bad AI formations; wants more realistic shapes.)
It seems fine to me. (Pushed four times for something to change; said no each time, then 'please stop asking this question'.)

responses.likenessWhy: It looked like an AI version of him. It wasn't an exact replica.
responses.storyWhy: It skipped a lot of in-between scenes and dialog but it was easy enough to follow.
responses.qualityWhy: It looked too much like it was created by AI.
responses.notGood: It was too AI created. It didn't look original or stylish. (Follow-ups: every page had the obvious AI look; give it a different style than the generic AI style; less cartoonish and mainstream.)

responses.likenessWhy: Facial hair and glasses carry the likeness, but the real head is narrower/longer than the drawn character's wider head.
responses.storyWhy: Images align with the text and the story matches Jack and the Beanstalk; the mother's face in the last picture looks too joyous for that moment.
responses.qualityWhy: Pleasant, but not store-quality; would expect a more whimsical hand-drawn approach.
responses.notGood: Head shape of the main character is inconsistent with the reference photo. (Follow-ups: expects more consistency when transposing a reference; a more whimsical hand-drawn or paintbrush style would feel less generic and higher quality.)

responses.likenessWhy: The glasses and facial hair totally nailed his real look
responses.storyWhy: It hit all the classic Jack and the Beanstalk story beats while keeping the custom character fun and easy to follow
responses.qualityWhy: Illustrations, colors and layout look really polished and fit right in with actual published picture books
responses.notGood: Make the story a bit longer. (Follow-ups: felt a bit rushed; could have used a slower pace with more detail.)

responses.likenessWhy: Similar face shape, facial hair and features.
responses.storyWhy: The words for the pictures ok
responses.qualityWhy: It's clearly AI generated, it doesn't have that quaint book look.
responses.notGood: Change the style of the images, instead of cartoony. (Follow-ups: something between cartoon and painting; 'just not so glossy'; the gloss makes it look cheap.)

responses.likenessWhy: He has the facial hair and the glasses on and the eyes look the same.
responses.storyWhy: It's familiar from when I read it as a child
responses.qualityWhy: It looks realistic and everything seems natural
responses.notGood: The detail could be better because it doesn't look HD. (Follow-ups: could be sharper; the land in the background was blurry and could have been brighter; a nicer view would make it easier to get into.)

excluded.reason: Finished in Engage after 21 minutes but timed out in Connect, so not one of the 10 paid. Scores likeness 4, story 2, professional 1, pay no. Notable: the words felt disjointed and lacked context ('Milky-White' is never explained); poor text is the top problem; 'numerous obvious visual errors'.
Returned the study at question 10 (not paid).
Returned the study at the start (not paid).
